spatial_claims.claim: Point C lies on segment AB, dividing it into segments AC and CB
BC is treated as an uncut line; AB is the line cut into segments AC and CB at C
Segment addition: AB consists of AC + CB (implicit from applying Prop 2.1 with AB cut at C)

configuration_map: Minimal configuration: a single line segment AB with an interior point C. Point A is the left endpoint, point B is the right endpoint, and C lies between them on the segment. This creates two sub-segments AC and CB such that AB = AC + CB. No auxiliary points or geometric figures are constructed. The proof operates entirely on rectangle and square areas derived from these segments.
pass_reason: The proof is primarily algebraic, applying Proposition 2.1 (a distributive identity for rectangles over segment sums) and the definition of a square. The only spatial claim is the given condition that C lies on AB, which is never contradicted. No geometric constructions, angle decompositions, inside/outside claims, or ray orderings appear. All spatial claims are trivially consistent.
